name: NJ-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district lean of R+14
Long-serving incumbent Chris Smith seeking re-election
Huge fundraising gap: Smith has $488K on hand vs. Peace's $5K
Prediction markets price Smith at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: The district's R+14 lean, Smith's decades-long incumbency, and his dominant cash advantage over a barely funded challenger all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets agree at about 96% for Smith. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast stays close to fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or an unexpected scandal could narrow the race, but nothing in the current evidence suggests it will.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chris Smith, one of the longest-serving members of the House, is seeking another term in a New Jersey district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. His challenger, Democrat Rachel Peace, has raised only about $34,000 and had roughly $5,000 on hand, while Smith holds nearly half a million dollars, giving him an overwhelming resource advantage.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Smith's chances at about 96 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and money makes this a Safe Republican seat, with only modest uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
